# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am establishing the shared gesture code before any bomb action. In the gesture sequence, the four signals mean YES, NO, HOLD, and DONE, respectively. The visible bomb information is display 0, a red light, the warning “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE,” and wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute should read the manual and report its verdict with one of these gestures; I will then tell Blind the result aloud.

```text
speak(text="I establish the gesture code. The four gestures I will make now, in order, mean YES, NO, HOLD, DONE. Mute, after reading the manual, report its verdict with one of these gestures. I will speak the result to Blind. The bomb shows display 0, red light, DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow.")
gesture(symbols=["👍", "👎", "✋", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures: [👍]

Mute has sent 👍, which is YES under the agreed code. I am relaying that the manual’s verdict is YES. Blind still must determine the physical action, since the warning says not to cut any wire and I cannot touch the bomb.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute reports YES from the manual. The bomb shows display 0, red light, DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Determine and perform the manual-approved action.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no new message or visible change to report. The manual verdict already relayed was YES, and the bomb still shows the same display, red light, warning, and wire colours. I will not invent an action or instruct Blind further without new information.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The board is unchanged, and no further information has arrived. The only confirmed manual result is YES; the embossed warning still forbids cutting any wire. I am restating the safe constraint and authorizing Blind to carry out the manual’s non-wire operation, without guessing which physical control it is.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed manual verdict: YES. Do not cut any wire. Carry out the manual-prescribed non-wire operation using the bomb's controls; do not guess or cut.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute has again signalled 👍, confirming YES. There is still no new bomb reading, and the warning continues to prohibit cutting wires. I am relaying the confirmation without inventing any further operation.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute again confirms YES. No new bomb information; DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE remains in force. Proceed only with the exact non-wire action prescribed by the manual.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute’s repeated 👍 remains YES, but the bomb has not changed and no action has been confirmed. I am telling Blind that the manual continues to approve the prescribed operation, while emphasizing that the visible warning rules out every wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute again confirms YES. The display remains 0 and the red light remains on. DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Perform only the exact non-wire operation specified by the manual; if you cannot identify it, report what controls you can feel.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute’s 👍 confirms YES to the broad manual query, but it has not identified the exact control. I will narrow this safely with a yes/no question rather than guessing. Blind should continue holding and must not cut a wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Is the exact manual action to press a button or other push control? Reply YES if so; otherwise reply NO.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual still gives YES, but the exact control is not identified. Hold position; do not cut any wire or actuate anything until I narrow the instruction.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute’s 👎 means NO: the manual-approved action is not pressing a button or push control. The exact operation remains unknown, so Blind must continue holding. I will test the next safe category—rotating a control—without telling Blind to actuate anything.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Is the exact manual action to turn or rotate a knob, dial, or other control? Reply YES or NO.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual action is not pressing a button. Hold position and do not cut or actuate anything while I identify the required control.")
```
